hypothesis: Among comparable-area regions, oceanic islands (volcanic islands never connected to a continent) hold fewer vascular plant species than continental or mainland regions of equal area, and this holds after controlling for physical conditions (latitude, climate, elevation range).
pass_criterion: Fit log10(species richness) ~ log10(area) + island/mainland type on GIFT checklists with complete floras. Pass if the oceanic-island intercept is lower than the mainland intercept by at least 0.30 log10 units (about half the richness) with a 95% CI excluding 0, AND the effect stays below -0.15 log10 units with CI excluding 0 after adding mean annual temperature, annual precipitation, absolute latitude and elevation range as covariates. Also pass only if, in area-matched bins (within 20% of each other, at least 30 pairs per bin), the median oceanic-island richness is below the median mainland richness in at least 80% of the bins covering 10 to 100,000 km2.
fail_criterion: Fail if the oceanic-island versus mainland intercept difference is under 0.15 log10 units or its 95% CI includes 0, or if the covariate-adjusted difference is not significantly negative, or if fewer than 50% of the area-matched bins show lower island median richness.
interpretation: Darwin's 'species of all kinds' is not testable across all taxa, so it is measured as native vascular plant species richness, the group GIFT covers best (a modern restriction, stated openly). 'Oceanic islands' means GIFT islands flagged as oceanic (volcanic or never land-connected), excluding continental-shelf and fragment islands. 'Equal continental areas' means mainland regions in GIFT (political units and biogeographical regions) with matching area, using only mainland checklists flagged as native and complete. 'Not explained by physical conditions' becomes a regression in which island type keeps a negative effect after controlling for climate, latitude and topography. The comparison uses only native species. Area is in km2.

dataset.name: GIFT – Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.publisher: Biodiversity, Macroecology & Biogeography group, University of Göttingen (Weigelt, König & Kreft)
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT holds native vascular plant checklists for about 2,282 islands and up to 1,345 mainland regions. Each region has area, an island/mainland flag, island geological origin (oceanic vs continental) and environmental variables. It is reachable through the GIFT R package (CRAN), e.g. GIFT_checklists(), GIFT_env() and GIFT_richness(). Fields used: entity_ID, geo_entity_ref, area, island/mainland type, island origin, native species richness, mean annual temperature, precipitation, latitude, elevation range. The database itself has no DOI; the DOI 10.1111/jbi.13623 belongs to the descriptive paper (Weigelt, König & Kreft 2020, J. Biogeogr. 47:16–43).
